newsitem.title: UK: EIB may revise the way it issues bonds -Karsenti.
newsitem.headline: EIB may revise the way it issues bonds -Karsenti.

text.p: The European Investment Bank will re-examine the way in which its bonds are sold to investors with a view to possibly changing the process in the period leading to EMU and afterwards, a senior EIB official said on Tuesday.
EIB director general of finance Rene Karsenti told bankers at a conference here: "We will look at the techniques adopted by sovereigns to sell bonds."
"That is not to say we are going to go straight to auctioning bonds," he added.
On Monday, the EIB, the European Union's main financing arm, was handed the task of lending to firms involved in high technology to boost jobs growth within the EU.
The bank was asked to examine the establishment of a facility for the financing of high-technology projects of small and medium-sized enterprises in cooperation with the European Investment Fund.

"It was another demonstration of the EIB's special and privileged role in Europe," Karsenti said, adding the EIB would now be among the five largest borrowers in Europe after EMU, including sovereigns.
Karsenti also said the EIB would launch more euro-tributary transactions in the run-up to EMU. "We have launched deals in four (EMU) currencies so far this year. There will be more."

Euro-tributary deals, or parallel bonds, are bonds launched in more than one currency but with the same coupon and maturity date. They contain clauses which allow for their redenomination into euros after EMU.

The third stage of European economic and monetary union, including the introduction of the European Union's planned single currency, the euro, is prescribed by EU law to take place no later than January 1, 1999.
